help.backups.hint: Credentials are encrypted in the settings of the respective database component and tied to the portable Drageon installation. Drageon always uses the tools supplied by the active version. Tables, SQL queries, users, permissions, and structural changes remain the responsibility of phpMyAdmin.
help.backups.text: Database Backups can save one, several, or all user databases from the active MySQL or MariaDB server. A separate SQL dump is created for each database under data/backups/databases. After explicit confirmation, a selected backup can be restored into a deliberately chosen target database or deleted.
help.backups.title: Database backups and restore
help.components.hint: Running versions must be stopped first. When deleting an active stopped version, Drageon warns whether another installed version will be selected or the component will become inactive. MariaDB and MySQL use an exclusive group from their manifests. phpMyAdmin, Composer, cURL and Node.js are optional tools.
help.components.text: Components are grouped into servers, PHP, databases and development tools. All bundled JSON package definitions remain in app/packages; their installed versions under bin/<component>/<version> can be removed individually. Add packages with New and edit them with the pencil button.
help.components.title: Components and Versions
help.cron.example:
[
  {
    "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
    "name": "Project cron every five minutes",
    "type": "PhpScript",
    "expression": "*/5 * * * *",
    "target": "www/myproject/cron.php",
    "arguments": "",
    "enabled": true,
    "catchUpMissedRun": false
  }
]
help.cron.hint: Targets for PHP scripts and commands can be entered or selected with Browse. The dialog opens the existing target's directory when possible, otherwise www. Files inside the Drageon directory are stored as portable relative paths; external files are not accepted. Large output is stored in full under app/var/logs/cron and summarized in the interface. Missed executions can run once after the next startup as soon as the web server is running. Settings can show a notification-area message and optionally play a sound when a cron job finishes; failures use a distinct warning sound.
help.cron.text: Cron jobs run only while Drageon is open. Supported types are PHP script, URL, cURL, and command. An expression has five fields: minute, hour, day, month, and weekday.
help.cron.title: Configuring Cron Jobs
help.logs.text: Logs contain application messages and process output. Database messages marked [Note] are normal information, not errors. Individual lines can be selected; all visible filtered messages can also be copied, and the app/var/logs directory can be opened directly. The view and log files can be cleared separately. In Settings, you can choose whether Drageon keeps running in the notification area or exits completely when the window is closed. The separate Exit Drageon menu item closes the app directly at any time. In the tray, Menu opens individual app pages. Go to offers localhost, phpMyAdmin (only when installed and active), and PowerShell. All servers can be started, stopped, or restarted from the tray and taskbar menus. Open PowerShell and Exit Drageon are also available from the app icon's context menu.
help.logs.title: Diagnostics and Tray
help.mail.example:
SMTP host: 127.0.0.1
SMTP port: 1025
Encryption: none
Username/password: empty
help.mail.hint: The inbox shows text, HTML source, headers, raw data, and attachments. All messages are stored portably under data/mail. A notification area message and optional sound for newly captured test emails can be enabled independently under Settings.
help.mail.text: Configure the application under test to use SMTP host 127.0.0.1 and the SMTP port selected under Settings. The default is 1025; TLS and authentication remain disabled. Add the following to php.ini:
help.mail.title: Configuring Test Emails
help.php.hint: Put custom INI directives in the text field. The active PHP version and its generated INI are used by the server, cron jobs and portable PowerShell. With Nginx, Drageon starts and monitors php-cgi.exe on 127.0.0.1. Restart the server after INI changes.
help.php.text: The original INI of the selected PHP version serves as the complete base. Settings, extensions, generated php.ini, and OPcache are managed separately for each PHP version. Files under bin/php remain unchanged.
help.php.title: PHP Settings
help.projects.hint: Project snapshots save files, dotfiles, empty folders, and links without copying their targets, plus the optional database, project metadata, and virtual host under data/snapshots. Saving the current state before a restore is enabled by default. Staging can only be created from a main project. Drageon copies files, links, and optionally the database and virtual host, but does not alter CMS configuration; after copying a database, update the staging database connection manually. Deleting a staging instance also deletes all of its snapshots.
help.projects.text: The project list is derived exclusively from the existing folders under www. projects.json contains only optional metadata such as favorites, URL, virtual host, database assignment, and staging relationship. Assign database selects an existing user database on the active MySQL or MariaDB server; a matching name is only a suggestion. The display name can be changed in the Snapshots and Staging dialog without renaming the project folder.
help.projects.title: Projects, snapshots, and staging
help.quick.hint: With HTTP port 80, the start page is available at http://localhost/. The general Drageon PowerShell starts in the app directory; a project's PowerShell button uses that project directory. Both automatically load the active PHP version, generated php.ini, and every component enabled for the portable PATH. Quick Access items can be enabled or disabled under Settings.
help.quick.text: 1. Install the desired versions under Components. 2. Activate the versions. 3. Start servers separately or together. 4. Place projects as folders under www.
help.quick.title: Quick Start
help.server.hint: phpMyAdmin does not have its own database password. With cookie authentication, enter the username and password of an account on the active database server on the login page. Users can then be managed under User accounts.
help.server.text: Choose Apache or Nginx in Settings → Server and configure the FastCGI port there. Apache remains the default. Component settings buttons open advanced Apache and phpMyAdmin settings. Nginx uses a generated nginx.conf and shared virtual host data.
help.server.title: Servers and phpMyAdmin
help.subtitle: Using and configuring the portable development environment.
help.title: Help
help.vhosts.apacheExample:
# Apache – additional configuration
SetEnv APP_ENV development
Header always set X-Robots-Tag "noindex, nofollow"
<FilesMatch \.php$>
    SetEnv PHP_VALUE "display_errors=1"
</FilesMatch>
help.vhosts.hint: .localhost names work without a hosts file. Other server names require external name resolution. The JSON file follows the complete host name and is renamed when it changes. Paths inside the app directory are stored as portable relative paths.
help.vhosts.text: Virtual hosts combine a host name and server name, for example website + localhost = website.localhost. DocumentRoot and enabled state appear below; the advanced section provides a port and extra settings per server.
help.vhosts.title: Virtual Hosts
